title: רב אשי
author: Heilprin source tradition; Warsaw digital witness

paragraphs: (a) Dinei Mamonot calls him Rabbana Ashi. He headed Sura’s academy, Mata Mechasya, Shabbat 11: “I acted so that Mata Mechasya would not be destroyed.” The Bavli says it was destroyed, though for a different reason. Heilprin says Ashi raised the synagogue above the houses. Rashi says he headed the academy and prevented the residents from raising their houses above the synagogue. Maharit: Bava Batra’s beginning says Ashi saw synagogue damage and brought his bed in, etc.; when demolishing and rebuilding, he raised it above the houses.

(b) Kiddushin 72b: on Rava’s death day Ashi was born—the true reading. Maimonides says Ashi received from Rava, understanding it like Shmuel and Eli: before Eli’s sun set, Shmuel’s rose, and Shmuel received from Eli. Ra'avad agrees with our reading and no reception from Rava. Halikhot Olam and She'erit Yosef 34b think Maimonides read “before it set”: before Rava could depart, Ashi was born to replace him. Berakhot 15, Ravina speaking to Rava, and Ellu Tereifot 46 support that reading: Ravina was Ashi’s student-colleague and saw Rava; presumably Rava also saw Ashi. End quotation. See my contrary evidence in the rules. See part I, 4099, 4113, 4127: born 4113, began heading the academy at fourteen, died 4187 or 4246 [thousand 4 carried from the context]. Chiddushei Aggadot, Bava Metzia, Hapo'alim: Ashi slightly older than Ravina. See my contradiction in the rules’ introduction.

(c) Gittin 59a; Dinei Mamonot 36a: from Rabbi until Ashi, Torah and greatness were never united. Even Huna bar Natan, greatest of his generation in Torah, and Marimar and Mar Zutra, Yuchasin’s Sherira epistle, submitted to him. Berakhot 57a: a goose in a dream presages wisdom. Ashi: “I saw one and had intercourse with it, and rose to greatness.” Ashi said that he entered the marsh, hung a tablet, and barked. Heilprin connects the dream to Ashi’s becoming academy head, like Rav Pappa. He saw leafy turnips and grew rich (I did not find it: Rav saw that). Israel had respite in his days. Mo'ed Katan 28a: the Angel of Death came; Ashi requested thirty days to review, “Happy is one arriving here with his learning in hand.” After thirty days it returned: he must die, for Huna bar Natan’s feet pressed onward, and reigns do not overlap even a hairbreadth.

(d) He blinded himself (see Rav Yosef). He entrusted his slave Minyamin to Ravina and Acha bar Rava for immersion, preventing self-acquisition as free, Yevamot 46a. Rafram compelled him to pay for a debt-document burned in youth, see there. Beitzah 6a: Rav Assi (should be Ashi, as Asheri) was distressed at omitting eruv tavshilin. Ravina asked why; Mordekhai addressed Ravina, etc.

(e) A version makes him marry Rami bar Abba’s daughter—not true; see there, requiring examination. Beitzah 29b: Ashi says “ours”—Rashi, my wife—“is Rami bar Chama’s daughter.” Yuchasin’s gloss at ש״ש [siglum unresolved] says so, forgetting Yuchasin under resh calls Rami bar Chama Chisda’s son-in-law and Ashi’s father-in-law, citing this passage. I find difficulty. Ashi’s wife sifted flour on a table’s back. “Ours is Rami bar Chama’s daughter, a man meticulous in conduct; she would not do so without seeing it at her parents’.” End quotation. To know Father’s conduct, presumably she was no younger than ten while he lived. Some evidence: Jerusalem Sanhedrin 7:2, Elazar son of Tzadok’s childhood observation of burning a priest’s daughter; the narrator notes he was at least ten; see there. Bava Batra 12b: prophecy after destruction goes to fools and children. Chisda’s daughter sat in his lap with Rava and Rami bar Chama before him. “Which do you want?” “Both.” Rava: “I shall be last.” Thus they were age-peers. Berakhot 48a: Abaye and Rava sat before Rabbah. He asked, “Whom do we bless?” They replied, “The Merciful One.” “And where does the Merciful One dwell?” Rava pointed to the roof; Abaye went outside and pointed toward heaven. Rabbah said, “You will both be sages.” Thus people say, “Gourds are known from their stalks.” Thus young age-peers (see Rava). Yevamot 34b: Rava married Chisda’s daughter ten years after her husband Rami bar Chama’s death. Berakhot 47b: Rami died young, in Rava’s lifetime. There 56a: bar Hedya interpreted dreams. Abaye paid him and said, “It was read to us: ‘Your sons and daughters given to another people.’” He replied, “You have many sons and daughters. You say, ‘I shall marry them to my relatives’; your wife says, ‘To my relatives,’ and compels you, so it is as though to another people.” Rava did not pay him. He told him his wife would die and her sons and daughters would come under another wife, etc. Later paid, he interpreted Abaye’s fallen palace and its dust covering Rava: Abaye dies, his academy comes to Rava. Walking with him, Rava found a fallen book saying dreams follow interpretation. “Wicked man, it depended on you and you tormented me! I forgive all but Chisda’s daughter”—his wife; see at length. Rosh Hashanah 18: Abaye lived sixty; Rava reigned fourteen afterward. Ashi was born on Rava’s death day and at least thirteen at marriage. Rami’s daughter was ten before her father died; ten years later Rava married her mother, making her twenty. This marriage and children preceded Abaye’s death. Add Rava’s fourteen-year reign and Ashi’s thirteen: she was over fifty. Hard to believe thirteen-year-old Ashi married a woman over fifty. Even if very young at Father’s death, learning his customs through her mother’s practice, she would still be over forty at marriage. Requires examination.

(f) He compiled the Babylonian Talmud, Sefer Hammitzvot’s view; Tosafot, beginning of Chullin and Shabbat; Rashi, Hassokher et Hapo'alim: Ashi ends authoritative instruction. He made recensions, Mi Shemet 157b: Ravina mentions Ashi’s first recension. Arukh, hadar, citing Chananel: received tradition, two annual study months, Adar and Elul, complete the cycle in thirty years (Yuchasin erroneous); then repeat. “Rav Assi” [אסי, as printed] remained long as academy head, sixty years. Heilprin calls the sixty-year lifespan a scribal error and attributes it to Rashba. The checked commentary with that wording is Rashbam. He completed the Talmud twice. First recension: the first acquired; second: divide, and law is divide—so should be read. Thus recension means repetition. Maimonides’ Zera'im introduction: thirty-five tractates of Ashi’s work survive. Maimonides also dates its compilation in Shinar to about a hundred years after the Jerusalem Talmud’s compilation; requires examination.

(g) Kahana the priest was his teacher; see many reports there. Yosef Tov Elem, commandment 48: law favors Ravina. Rosh, Kiddushin 1:16 [Heilprin cites chapter 8, 28b], and Halakhot Gedolot agree; see Chut Hashani, section 78. Chavvot Yair: perhaps the Land’s air benefited Ravina. R.Y. [ר״י; authority unresolved] favors Ashi. Halikhot Olam: Ravina his student-colleague, Megillah 26b; end of Mo'ed Katan’s first chapter; Menachot 42a. Tosafot, Shabbat 9b, favors Ashi, later than Acha bar Yaakov. Rosh and Tosafot, Bava Metzia, chapter 1: Ashi over Mar Zutra. Bava Metzia 16a, 48b: later, greater in wisdom and number. Common saying, “Ashi’s statement is an invention”: Pesachim 11a; Yevamot 21a; Zevachim 100b; Menachot 68a, 95b; Bava Metzia 71b; Arukh, bad.

(h) There is an early Ashi in Rav’s time and a late Ashi; determine teacher/student by generations. My רא״ק means early Ashi, רא״א late Ashi. Below [E] and [L] reproduce those assignments. Rabbi Abba spoke to him—three Abbas, requiring examination; Abbahu objected—two, requiring examination. Bar Avin and bar Kippuk contemporary [L]. Adda finds Ashi’s view reasonable [E]. Adda bar Chavu before him [L]; Rav Adda bar Rava spoke to him [L]; Adda the elder before him [L]. Acha bar Acha and Acha of Perzaki spoke to him; Rav Acha. Acha bar Rav Avira in his name [E]; Acha bar Avya spoke to him [E]; Acha the elder [E]; Acha bar Abba spoke to him [E]; Acha of Hutzal before him [L]. Acha bar Ika spoke to him; Acha bar Rav Ashi. Acha bar Adda spoke to him [E]. He sent Acha bar Ravina seventeen zuz for firstborn redemption [L]. Acha bar Chiyya spoke to him; Acha bar Rav Yosef spoke to him [L]. Bar Ivo contemporary; Ika bar Chanina; Ittai in his days. Ammi bar Abba in his name. He asked Amemar, calling him master [L]. Rav Assi spoke to him [E]. Ashi of Avira contemporary. Bavehu spoke to him (I did not find it); Rav Budya spoke to him. Bibi in his name. Gevaya of Bei Ketil before him; Geviha of Argiza. Gamda spoke to him; Huna bar Chayyun spoke to him; Huna Mar before him. Huna bar Avya spoke to him and appeared in his dream. Before Huna, who asked him [E]. Mar Huna bar Nachman spoke to him. Huna bar Avin’s sons before him; Huna bar Mar Zutra contemporary. Huna bar Rava spoke to him; Huna Mar bar Rava of Perzakya spoke to him. He spoke to Hoshaya (another reading Yehoshua) bar Rav Idi. Hillel, colleague. Zevid of Nehardea’s daughter-in-law came before him. Zevida spoke to him. Rav Zuti contemporary; Mar Zutra, colleague; Mar Zutra bar Rishba contemporary; Mar Zutra bar Mari bar Issur. Chaviva the Mechozan spoke to him. Chiyya bar Abba [E]; Chanilai the Mechozan spoke to him. Chanina in his name [E]; Chanina bar Bibi bar Abaye contemporary; Chanin. Chanan bar Rava spoke to him [E]; Rav Chanin spoke to him. Chinena bar Kahana in his name [E]; Yehudah in his name [E], see there. In Yehoshua ben Levi’s name, see there; Yochanan’s name, Zevachim 11b; Beitzah 37b. Yose bar Avin went to study with him. Yeimar spoke to him. In Yannai bar Yishmael’s name. Yitzchak bar Mesharshya contemporary. Yirmeyah spoke to him, Zevachim 15b [E]—requires examination. He visited Rav Kahana [E]; Kahana the priest, his teacher. In Minyomi bar Nachumi’s name. Minyamin, his slave. Mari bar Pinchas bar Rav Chisda before him. He spoke to Rav Mari; Mari bar Issur the convert; Mari bar Isak contemporary. Mar Yenuka and Mar Kashisha spoke to him; Mar bar Amemar spoke to him. He spoke to Mar bar Rav Yosef [L]; Mar Kashisha son of Rava spoke to him. Mar son of Rav Ashi, or Mari. Mordekhai, his student—requires examination. He taught before Rav Mattana [E]; before Nachman (bar Yitzchak, Tosafot), Menachot 102a [L]—requires examination. Rav Nechemyah R.G. [ר״ג; title unresolved] asked him. Natan bar Mar Zutra spoke to him. Sima bar Rav Idi to Ashi; Sama bar Rav Mesharshya; Sama bar Rav Ashi spoke to him. Rav Avira in his name. In Ulla’s name [E]; Ukvan of Meshan spoke to him [E]. He spoke to Pinchas bar Ammi. Pappi, his teacher. Pappa spoke to him, Avodah Zarah 40a [L]. Bar Kippak, his student. In Rav’s name [E]; Rava’s name, Chullin 17b [L]. “Rava told Ashi,” Ketubbot 111a, is an error; Ein Yaakov has Ravina. Rava of Barnish to Ashi. He visited Rava bar Chinena. Rabbah in Ashi’s name, Chullin 76a [E]. He told Rabbah, “Did not Ulla say?”, Me'ilah 3, end of b; Bava Kamma 114b [E]. Rabbah of Perzaki spoke to him; Rabbah bar Mari before him. Rabbah bar Rav Huna in Ashi’s name [E]; Rabbah Zuti spoke to him. In Rabbi’s name, Gittin 39, end of b [E]. Ravin of Naresh healed his daughter. Ravin bar Chinena spoke to him. Ravina, student-colleague [L]; Ravina Zuti before him. Rafram before him. In Shabbatai’s name [E]. Shila of Shilanya spoke to him. He taught before Rav Shimi. Rav Shemen spoke to him. In Resh Lakish’s name, Bekhorot 25, end of a [E]. Rav Sheshet of Kartiza visited Rav Ashi.
